IA-2025-HSB785.title: A bill for an act modifying the major economic growth attraction program, and including effective date provisions.

actions.text: Introduced, referred to Ways and Means.
Subcommittee: Nordman, Bloomingdale, Holt, Jacoby and Judge.
Committee report approving bill, renumbered as HF 2801.

IA-2025-HSB785.policyArea: business assistance, major economic growth attraction program, tax credits
IA-2025-HSB785.aiSummary: The bill would change Iowa’s major economic growth attraction program for business projects that get tax credits. It would add a special tax credit for one eligible business in a rural county, allow some of these credits to be transferred to another person or company with state approval, and set rules for repayment if the business does not follow the program. It also would define terms like “rural county” and “affiliate,” and it includes effective date provisions.

IA-2025-SF2488.title: A bill for an act relating to early childhood and family services, including the creation of an early childhood and family services system, making appropriations, convening an early childhood Iowa interim study committee, and including applicability, retroactive applicability, and effective date provisions.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by President and Speaker, and sent to Governor.
Read first time, passed on file.

IA-2025-SF2488.policyArea: appropriations, boards, commissions, and councils, child assistance
IA-2025-SF2488.aiSummary: The law creates a statewide early childhood and family services system for children under 19 and their families, run by the state health and human services department. It sets up district plans and advisory councils, and it directs the department to use services such as family support, early help, and community resources to support healthy child development. It also includes money for the program and creates an interim study committee to review early childhood Iowa issues.

IA-2025-SF2422.aiSummary: The law changes rules for state public assistance programs, including SNAP, Medicaid, and the Iowa Health and Wellness Plan. It updates how the state checks citizenship and immigration status, changes SNAP income and eligibility rules for some noncitizens, and requires reports on SNAP payment error rates starting in the fiscal quarter that begins October 1, 2026. It also directs the department to seek federal waivers for SNAP benefit timing and verification rules, and changes Medicaid retroactive coverage rules for some people, with some parts taking effect January 1, 2027.

IA-2025-HF2799.title: A bill for an act relating to matters under the purview of the economic development authority, the utilities commission, and the department of education, including creation of the headquarters expansion and development for growth and employment program, and the business incentives for growth program training fund; repeal of the new jobs tax credit program; the major economic growth attraction program; load forecasting and analysis of electric transmission system expansion plans; creation of the electric transmission system expansion planning and analysis and load forecasting fund; the industrial new jobs training program; and establishing the new jobs training program interim study committee; and including effective date provisions.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by Speaker and President, and sent to Governor.
Read first time, attached to SF 2506.
Introduced, placed on Ways and Means calendar.

IA-2025-HF2799.policyArea: business incentives for growth program, economic development authority, education department
IA-2025-HF2799.aiSummary: The act changes programs under the economic development authority, the utilities commission, and the department of education. It creates a new headquarters expansion and growth program and a business training fund, and it repeals some older tax credit and training programs. It also changes electric transmission planning and creates a new fund for that work, and it sets up an interim study committee on job training.

IA-2025-HF2706.title: A bill for an act relating to judicial officers, including magistrate appointments in judicial election districts, senior magistrates, and judicial officer compensation, and including effective date provisions.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by Speaker and President, and sent to Governor.
Read first time, attached to SF 2401.
Placed on calendar under unfinished business.

IA-2025-HF2706.policyArea: judges and court officials, judicial elections, magistrates
IA-2025-HF2706.aiSummary: This act changes how Iowa magistrates are appointed and tracked in judicial election districts. It also changes rules for using district associate judges in place of magistrates, how magistrate pay is set, and what court officials must record and report. The law became Chapter 1063 and takes effect on the dates listed in the act.

IA-2025-HF2667.title: A bill for an act relating to project design standards and specifications, including by providing for a statewide urban design and specifications board and requiring certain reports to city councils regarding noncompliant projects.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by Speaker and President, and sent to Governor.
Placed on calendar under unfinished business.
Read first time, attached to SF 2394.

IA-2025-HF2667.aiSummary: The bill would create a statewide urban design and specifications board in the transportation department to set design and specs manuals for public projects. It would also require the board to post changes and an estimate of any cost changes from those updates. If a county or city approves a project plan that does not follow these standards, the local government would have to pay the extra costs, and property owners could not be billed for those costs.

IA-2025-HF2601.title: A bill for an act relating to campaign finance, including participation in ballot issue campaigns by foreign nationals and investigations of election misconduct, and making penalties applicable.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by Speaker and President, and sent to Governor.
Point of order raised on S-5203, ruled not germane.
Read first time, attached to SF 2204.
Placed on calendar under unfinished business.

IA-2025-HF2601.aiSummary: This law tightens Iowa campaign finance rules for ballot issue campaigns, which are efforts to pass or defeat a measure on the ballot. It bars foreign nationals from taking part in decisions about those campaigns or from asking others to give or spend money for them, and it requires certain donor affirmations in campaign reports. It also sets rules for investigations to protect donor privacy where possible and adds civil penalties of $10,000 or three times the amount involved, whichever is greater.

IA-2025-HF2199.title: A bill for an act relating to level II law enforcement academy training programs.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by Speaker and President, and sent to Governor.
Placed on calendar under unfinished business.
Read first time, referred to Judiciary.

IA-2025-HF2199.aiSummary: The law updates rules for level II law enforcement academy training programs in Iowa. It says people applying through the short-course level II program must show they finished a two-year or four-year police science or criminal justice program, or meet other academy rules, and they must be hired by a law enforcement agency within 18 months after finishing the program if they were not hired already.

IA-2025-SF2428.aiSummary: The law changes Iowa school rules on student discipline, special education, and staff duties. It affects school districts, charter schools, innovation zone schools, teachers, and students with special education plans or plans under section 504 of the federal Rehabilitation Act. It also orders the education department to make training on special education team rules, creates a pilot program for one rural and one urban district, and lets teachers ask for a student’s special education team meeting.

IA-2025-SF2086.title: A bill for an act authorizing schools to offer an elective junior fire fighter program to students enrolled in grades eleven and twelve.

actions.text: Reported correctly enrolled, signed by President and Speaker, and sent to Governor.
Subcommittee: Rinker, Kniff McCulla and McBurney.
Read first time, referred to Labor and Workforce.

IA-2025-SF2086.policyArea: emergency management, fire departments, fire service training bureau
IA-2025-SF2086.aiSummary: The law lets school districts and accredited nonpublic schools offer an elective junior fire fighter program to students in grades 11 and 12. The program must work with a local fire department and use training and curriculum approved by the fire service training bureau. It also sets what students under 18 may do and what they may not do, and it lets students who finish the program and meet other requirements take firefighter I certification testing, though the certification is not issued until age 18.

IA-2025-HF2757.title: A bill for an act relating to nuclear electric generation facilities by creating sales and use tax exemptions and refunds, making appropriations to the state board of regents for establishing and maintaining a nuclear energy workforce, making penalties applicable, and including applicability and retroactive applicability provisions.

House concurred in Senate amendment H-8428, as amended.

IA-2025-HF2757.policyArea: energy use, nuclear energy, radioactive materials
IA-2025-HF2757.aiSummary: The law creates sales and use tax breaks and refunds for nuclear electric generation facilities for work like site prep, construction, repairs, safe storage, and restarting a shut-down plant. It also sets up a state fund for nuclear energy workforce programs at state colleges and gives money to the Board of Regents for those programs. A facility that uses the tax break must make yearly payments to the fund and may have to repay the tax savings if it does not start or restart commercial operation within the set time.
